description: The Giant Puffball is a large, often soccer-ball-sized, smooth white spherical fungus that grows in meadows, pastures, and woodland edges. When young its interior is pure white and homogeneous, and it darkens to olive-brown as the powdery spore mass (gleba) matures. It is one of the largest fruiting bodies among fungi, sometimes reaching 50 cm or more across.
edibilityNotes: Edible only when young, with a firm, pure-white, completely homogeneous interior; it should be cooked. CRITICAL SAFETY: before eating ANY puffball, cut it vertically top to bottom. A true Giant Puffball shows uniform white flesh with no internal structure. If you see the silhouette of a developing capped, gilled mushroom inside, it is the egg/button stage of an Amanita (potentially the deadly Amanita phalloides, A. virosa, or A. ocreata) and must be discarded. If the cut interior shows any yellowing, gill-like patterning, or a tough/rooted central column, do not eat it. Once the interior begins to yellow, discolor, or turn olive-brown (spores maturing), it is no longer edible and may cause gastrointestinal upset.
distribution: Widespread across temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere, including North America and Europe.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Amanita button/egg stage (e.g. Amanita phalloides, A. virosa, A. ocreata)
dangerousLookalikes.note: Young egg-stage Amanita species can superficially resemble a small white puffball, but cutting them vertically reveals the silhouette of a developing cap, gills, and stem inside. Several of these Amanitas are deadly (amatoxin poisoning). Always slice every puffball top-to-bottom to confirm uniform, structureless white flesh.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Pigskin / earthball (Scleroderma species)
dangerousLookalikes.note: Earthballs can look puffball-like but have a thick, firm rind and a flesh that is purplish-black to dark even when young (not pure white and homogeneous). They are toxic and cause gastrointestinal poisoning; the dark interior at the cut distinguishes them from an edible young Calvatia.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Other Calvatia and Lycoperdon puffballs
dangerousLookalikes.note: Smaller true puffballs are also edible only when the interior is pure white and homogeneous; the same vertical-cut test applies to rule out Amanita buttons and to confirm immature, undiscolored gleba.
